summary: Phase 2 backend tests: 22/23 pass. All new endpoints verified: register-pending → login-blocked → admin/pending-users → approve (parent→approved, driver→active) → activate-parent (400 no kids, 400 no driver, 200 ready) → login-success → photo upload (user & child) → driver no_show creates parent notification → reject deletes user. critical.issue: Seeded parents cannot log in. Their user docs were inserted before the 'status' field existed (status=None), and the new login gate `u.get('status') != 'active'` rejects them with 403 'Awaiting driver assignment by admin'. The handoff note claimed auto-migration to status='active', but no migration code exists in server.py. Fix options: (a) one-shot startup migration `db.users.update_many({'status': {'$exists': False}}, {'$set': {'status': 'active'}})`, or (b) treat missing status as 'active' in the login check.

action_items: CRITICAL: Backfill status='active' for pre-existing seeded users so parent@vipkids.com and parent2@vipkids.com can log in. Recommended fix in on_startup(): `await db.users.update_many({'role': 'parent', 'status': {'$in': [None]}}, {'$set': {'status': 'active'}})` (or treat missing field as active in login check). Until this lands, the documented demo parent account is broken — the smoke-test in the handoff note must have been against a fresh DB only.
Optional: when seeding, every user should always include 'status' so future gates remain consistent.
Optional: lowercase comparison in admin/pending-users frontend if mixed-case emails are ever stored.

rca_of_issue: Bug: seeded parent login fails after Phase 2 changes. RCA: login() now enforces `if u.get('role') == 'parent' and u.get('status') != 'active': raise 403`. The seeded parent docs were inserted in a prior iteration WITHOUT a status field. Server seed is idempotent (skips when users exist) so the seed-time addition of `status: 'active'` in iteration 2 never runs on the live DB. Reproduction: `curl -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -d '{"email":"parent@vipkids.com","password":"parent123"}'` → 403. Mitigation: add a one-time migration in on_startup() before seed_demo_data: `await db.users.update_many({'role': 'parent', 'status': {'$exists': False}}, {'$set': {'status': 'active'}})` and same for drivers/admin for robustness.
